items.title: Tyler Herro scores 50, officials miss out-of-bounds call on Joel Embiid in 76ers' 132-129 win over Bucks
items.summary: Tyler Herro scored a career-high 50 points Saturday, but that wasn't enough for the Milwaukee Bucks to get their second win of the season in a 132-129 defeat to the Philadelphia 76ers. Milwaukee was deprived of an opportunity to take the lead in the closing seconds when officials missed Joel Embiid stepping out of bounds. Rookie Brayden Burries hit a corner 3-pointer for the Bucks to cut the Sixers' lead to 130-129. After a timeout, LeBron James threw an inbounds pass to Embiid, who attempted to dribble out the clock near the Milwaukee basket. Embiid stepped out of bounds at the baseline with his left foot, but the officials did not call the turnover and Herro was forced to foul. items.summary: Rockets head coach Ime Udoka didn’t hide his disgust for his team’s effort following Friday’s NBA Cup loss in Denver, according to Varun Shankar of The Houston Chronicle. Udoka called the Rockets “mentally fragile” and was particularly critical of the defense, saying it lacked physicality, effort and “attention to detail.” In a back-and-forth contest with 32 lead changes and 17 ties, Houston was up five points with 5:10 remaining but was outscored 23-9 to close out the game. “You got to compete on (the defensive) end to give yourself a chance. You score 124, you should be able to win,” Udoka said. “But just count out the quarters. They had four 30-point quarters… you’re not going to win anything and that just shows a lack of effort, attention to detail or fight on that end. items.summary: James Harden’s slow start to 2026/27 has led to some consternation in Cleveland, but the Cavaliers guard erupted for a season-high 51 points in Friday’s NBA Cup victory over Indiana, according to ESPN. Harden, who passed Kobe Bryant for the third-most 50-point games in NBA history with 26, is the fourth-oldest player to score 50-plus points in a game. The 37-year-old, who was plus-22 in 40 minutes, shot 15-of-26 from the field, including 7-of-11 from three-point range. He also made all 14 of his free throws in addition to having six rebounds and six assists. “That was vintage,” Cavs head coach Kenny Atkinson said. “You really can’t do anything if you’re the opposing coach. There’s nothing you can do, especially when he’s getting by you like that.
